admission.justification: Three fixture-card tests pin the own-then-base allocation order, the partner-number takeover and the injectivity of the maps, so a future allocation change that breaks the order fails before it lands.

applicability: Every both-changed card whose references were paired, in crossing syncs and ordinary converted-line syncs.
conditions: Pairing completed without a rule-7 skip.
Incoming keeps every number; fresh numbers start above all three sides' highest, own-represented groups first in own order, then base-only groups in base order.
exclusions: Cards merged without alignment under rule 7.
Non-reference collections, which merge by entry id.

evidence: Rationale: _partner_numbers gives every base/incoming pair's number to the base side and to its own partner, and every direct pair's number to the own side; _fresh_groups then emits exactly the unnumbered groups, own-represented first in own number order, base-only after in base number order; _assign_numbers numbers them from one above the highest of the three sides. An empty base contributes no groups, so both-added cards freshen in own order above the own/incoming maxima. Observed: test_fresh_numbers_follow_own_order_then_base_order pins base {1:5,2:7,3:3} own {1:5,4:6}; test_both_added_cards_align_distinct_references_without_collision pins incoming [1] own [2].

statement: Rule 3 fresh allocation: partner numbers are taken from incoming; every other group takes one fresh number above all three maxima, own-represented groups in own number order first, then base-only groups in base number order
